paragraphs: The R350 CDI uses the OM642 — a 3.0-litre V6 diesel that served as Mercedes' workhorse six-cylinder diesel across much of the late 2000s and early 2010s. It was fitted throughout the R-Class's entire production run from 2006 to 2013, across both the W251 (standard wheelbase) and V251 (long wheelbase) chassis. The OM642 is a robust engine, but one with a well-documented pattern of swirl flap and injector wear over time — which is precisely what we address as standard on every rebuild.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every R350 CDI on the road.

cards.body: A 3.0-litre inline-six petrol mild-hybrid engine fitted to the R350 CDI from 2023 to present. The M256 features an integrated starter-generator (ISG) and electric auxiliary compressor, making it a more modern and efficient design than the older M276 V6. We replace timing chains, bearings, water pump and gaskets as standard on every M256 rebuild.

compatibility.intro: Because the R350 CDI uses the M256 — a different engine from the V8 units in the GT 63 range — fitting the wrong replacement or assuming parts from other R-Class variants will work risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:
